atAGlance: Bò xào lúc lắc is wok-tossed shaking beef pieces, usually with onion, bell pepper, rice, and lime-pepper salt.
whatItIs: Bò xào lúc lắc is shaking beef: wok-tossed beef cubes with onion, garlic, pepper, and a savory glaze, usually served with lime-pepper salt, salad, or rice.
howToEnjoy: Dip beef cubes lightly in lime-pepper salt and eat while the wok-seared edges are hot. Rice or salad balances the beef richness.
howLocalsOrder: Order bò xào lúc lắc as a shared plate or rice companion. Ask for less onion, less pepper, or lime-pepper salt on the side.
worthKnowing: In Vietnamese restaurants, lúc lắc refers to the shaking wok motion, a useful clue that the beef comes cubed and seared.
goodToKnow: The wok glaze should cling to the beef cubes and vegetables. Use lime-pepper salt as the bright accent, not as a separate heavy dip.
